body:
Refs #11519. This partial repair covers the `ArrayBuffer`-family `toString` residual left open by #11627. When `ArrayBuffer`, `SharedArrayBuffer`, or `DataView` reaches the shared Buffer dispatcher, its inherited `Object.prototype.toString` behavior must ignore every argument. The dispatcher now sends these non-indexed byte views through the canonical object-tag path before Buffer encoding and range handling. Buffer's own encoding behavior remains unchanged.

The regressions cover no argument, runtime-built short and literal encodings, extra range arguments, throwing coercion, and Buffer controls. A direct dispatcher test checks byte-view brands with short and heap encoding values and keeps the Buffer hex path as a control.

At `5e41d1d8b19c030754975afeca52a9c277eda739`, the coherent dev build of `perry`, `perry-runtime-static`, and `perry-stdlib-static` passed. The focused direct runtime test passed (1 passed, 5,797 filtered out). The 18-case fixture compiled with `--no-auto-optimize` and with the default auto-optimization path; both outputs matched pinned Node 26.5.1. The auto-optimization run rebuilt the matching runtime and stdlib archives with the `async-bridge` feature, without fallback; an initial 180-second build timeout is retained in the evidence, and the longer retry passed.

Validation was performed on Linux. Full `scripts/run_lint_gates.sh` completed with exit 1: 30 of 137 commands failed and two CI-only commands were skipped. Twenty-eight failures reproduce the saved baseline (25 static/release checks and three warning/Clippy commands). The Windows xwin gate is blocked by proxy HTTP 403. The docs wrapper misses the external target directory; direct generation matches the earlier baseline-attributed outputs, including markdown drift against the tracked empty reference. Full lint is not claimed green. Custom `Symbol.toStringTag` overrides on registered byte-view receivers and typed-string `Symbol.iterator` identity remain outside this partial fix.
